xref.title: Founding and Location (1977)
xref.body: The Power Station, located in New York at approximately 53rd and 10th, was founded in 1977 by Tony Bongiovi, the second cousin of John Bon Jovi. The building previously served as a Consolidated Edison power plant and later a TV studio for "Let's Make a Deal." "In 1977, the building was bought and rebuilt as a recording studio by Tony Bongeovi, the second cousin of some New Jersey kid named John Bongeovi."

xref.title: Cremation and Burial (1979)
xref.body: Following his death, Sid Vicious's family reportedly struggled to find a New York funeral home willing to take his body. He was eventually cremated in Jersey, and his ashes were spread on Nancy Spungen's grave in Philadelphia. "Apparently the family couldn't find a New York funeral home that would take his body, so he ended up being cremated into Jersey. His ashes were apparently spread on Nancy Spungens grave in Philadelphia."

xref.title: Founding and Shared Interests (1984)
xref.body: Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley, who formed the indie group Yo La Tengo in 1984, first met at shows and record shops in New Jersey. Their bond was solidified when they discovered a mutual fandom for the New York Mets baseball team. "Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley would see each other at the same shows at the same record shops in New Jersey. And when they realized they were both fans of the New York Mets, poor guys, that sealed the deal. Yolotengo started in 1984"

xref.title: Star-Spangled Banner Controversy and Frank Sinatra Feud (1990)
xref.body: In 1990, Sinead declined to have "The Star-Spangled Banner" played before a show in New Jersey, which was misconstrued as a refusal to perform if it was played. Upon hearing this, Frank Sinatra famously declared his desire to "kick her in the ass." "And when Frank Sinatra heard that, he famously said he would like to, quote, kick her in the ass."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: SNL Pope John Paul II Photo Tear (October 3, 1992) – Career-Ending Television Moment
xref.body: After a series of controversies (refusing to appear on SNL while Andrew Dice Clay was host in 1990; refusing the national anthem before a New Jersey show in August 1990; skipping the 1991 Grammys despite four nominations; a perceived pro-Saddam comment in March 1991), Sinead O'Connor appeared on *Saturday Night Live* on October 3, 1992, singing Bob Marley's "War." In rehearsal she held a picture of a refugee child; live, she substituted a photo of Pope John Paul II — taken from her mother's bedroom wall — and tore it up at the word "evil," saying "fight the real enemy." There was complete silence from the studio audience. NBC received nearly 5,000 complaints and the resulting media blowback permanently ended her mainstream career. The inspiration was Bob Geldof tearing up a picture of John Travolta on *Top of the Pops* in the 1970s. "NBC received almost 5,000 complaints. The blowback in the media was intense and her career never, ever recovered."

xref.title: Performance on Vote for Change Tour (2004)
xref.body: Eddie Vedder was invited on stage by Bruce Springsteen to perform "Better Man" during a last-minute added New Jersey show on October 13, 2004, as part of the "Vote for Change Tour," an event dedicated to influencing the 2004 US presidential election. "A New Jersey show was added at the last second on October the 13th, 2004. And Midway through the gig, Springsteen invited Eddie Vetteron stage to play Better Man."

xref.title: Public Pleas for Mental Health Help (2017)
xref.body: In the summer of 2017, Sinead went public on Facebook from a Travelodge room in New Jersey, stating she was still suicidal and frequently in and out of hospital psych wards. She later made genuine attempts to destigmatize mental illness through appearances on TV shows like Oprah and Dr. Phil. "The following summer, Shanade went public on Facebook from her room at a travel lodge in New Jersey, saying that she was still suicidal with only her doctor and psychiatrist standing in her way."

xref.title: Aggressive Powerpop Sound
xref.body: Hailing from New Jersey, The Smithereens were noted as one of the most aggressive-sounding Powerpop bands. Their sound blended powerful guitars with pop melodies; if the guitars were dialed down, what remained was essentially straightforward pop, highlighting their unique position within the genre. "Same thing with the Smitherines, a band from New Jersey, who was amongst the most aggressive sounding PowerPop bands."

xref.title: Assassination at El Rosa Villa Concert
xref.body: Dimebag Darrell, a revered guitarist from Pantera and Damageplan, was assassinated on December 8, 2004, exactly 24 years after John Lennon's death. During a Damageplan gig at the El Rosa Villa venue in Columbus, Ohio, attended by about 400 people, Nathan Gale rushed the stage and shot Darrell three times in the head at point-blank range as the band began their first song. "As the band started their first song at around 10-20 that night, a man named Nathan Gayle, 6'3", 250 pounds and wearing a Columbus Blue Jacket's hockey jersey, rushed the stage and shot Darryl with a 9mm semi-automatic pistol."

xref.title: Band Name Origin – From Neil Young Concert, Not Eddie's Grandmother's Jam
xref.body: The story about Eddie's fictional grandmother "Pearl" and her peyote jam is completely fabricated — acknowledged as a joke. The real story: the band needed to abandon their initial name "Mookie Blallock" (after the New Jersey Nets point guard) because his lawyers feared trademark confusion. While brainstorming a new name at a Seattle restaurant, everyone liked "Pearl." They went to New York for record-deal business, attended a Neil Young concert, were impressed by his long improvisational instrumental jams featuring competing creative visions, and settled on "Pearl Jam." Eddie later added a metaphorical layer: that competing creative irritants can come together into something great, like a pearl. "They found themselves in New York on business involving the brand-new major label record deal."

xref.body: Metal fans, including those attending Metallica shows, are noted for proudly wearing shirts of the bands on the bill, comparing it to wearing a home team's jersey at a sporting event. "Into a Metallica show? Count the shirts? Exactly."

xref.title: Formation and Style
xref.body: The Misfits were formed around 1976 by Glenn Danzig in New Jersey. They maintained their presence for six years, distinctively blending hardcore with themes from horror movies and elements of metal. "The Missfits were from Jersey. The main guy was Glenn Danzig, who started the band somewhere around 1976. Armed with his own indie record label. And as he kept the misfits going for six years, blending hardcore with horror movies and metal."

xref.title: Home Recordings (Early 1990s)
xref.body: This New Jersey-based band exemplified the lo-fi approach by recording their songs into a cheap machine that simply sat on top of their television. This rudimentary setup highlights their commitment to a raw, accessible, and unpolished recording process, characteristic of the emerging low-fidelity scene of the early 1990s. "In New Jersey, a band called Silver Juice, were recording their songs into a cheap machine that just kind of sat on top of their TV."

xref.title: Joey Ramone's Death and Memorial
xref.body: Diagnosed with lymphoma in 1995, Joey Ramone's cancer worsened after he broke his hip in a fall in late 2000, which necessitated coming off his chemotherapy. He died on April 15, 2001, just one month before his 50th birthday. The corner of East Second Street and Bowery, near CBGB and his last apartment, is now officially named "Joey Ramone Place." He is buried in Hillside Cemetery in New Jersey, overlooking Manhattan. "he died on April 15, 2001, a month short of his 50th birthday. The corner of East Second Street in Bahri is now officially known as Joey Ramon Place."

"Would prohibit entry to minors at concerts by Marilyn Manson, Rob Zombie, or Korn."

xref.title: The Teapot Incident
xref.body: Backstage at the Capitol Theater in Passaic, New Jersey, Joey Ramone, suffering from a cold, rigged a makeshift humidifier using a teapot on a hot plate in the dressing room. The teapot "ended up blowing up in Joey's face," causing second and third-degree burns. Despite his injuries, he was rushed to the hospital for treatment and then returned to the venue to perform the show. "Somehow it ended up blowing up in Joey's face and engsculting water all over him."

xref.title: Tom Wally's Unusual Meeting
xref.body: When Warner Brothers President Tom Wally wanted to meet Billy Talent, he refused to leave his New Jersey beach house. The band was flown to New Jersey, played a "s***ly little session" in a rented airplane hanger with unfamiliar gear, while Wally sat looking at the floor, preoccupied with his house. After the performance, he still wanted to sign them but only allowed them to eat on his patio during a family birthday, providing fried chicken and beer. "Tom Wally had, he wanted to see us. He was the president of Warner Brothers. And he didn't want to leave his beach house in New Jersey to come to the city. So they took us to New Jersey, rented an airplane hanger. We played the s***ly little session in front of him."
